name: Rich Purple
lede: Rich Purple is a modifier name, "rich" attached to the parent color [[purple]], a phrase color books use for the deepest, most saturated purples.

sections.title: A modifier, not a fixed name
sections.body:
The name follows one of the library's most common patterns: the modifier "rich" placed in front of the parent color, [[purple]] [1]. This exact label is first recorded in 2010, in the xkcd color survey, a large, informal internet survey in which hundreds of thousands of visitors typed their own name for a swatch; the library keeps names that enough people typed the same way [1][4]. The phrase "rich purple" itself has long been used descriptively before that survey, outside any naming system: historians use it for the deep purples of murex-dye and archil-dye textiles and for glaze effects achieved by painting a red lake over a blue ground [2][3]. The hex #720058 is a screen approximation only, not a measured dye or pigment [1].

Its nearest library look-alike is [[velvet]], about 2.7 units away in LCH space, read as almost the same color [1].

Other close matches in the library include [[grape]], duller, and [[cellini]], more vivid and lighter [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The automated archive tool used for this project could not compute a usable match count for this hex, so no painting-archive figures are given here [5]. The swatch should be read only as a screen approximation.

openers: Rich Purple's exact label dates to a 2010 internet survey, though the phrase itself is far older.

issues: Fixed mis-cited chapter: the red-lake-over-blue glaze claim is in Bright Earth ch. 13, not ch. 11 (ch. 11 covers ancient Egyptian/Mesopotamian pigment chemistry, unrelated). Verified archil claim against St Clair ch. 76, which matches.
